title: lvm on linux: a filesystem is full but the volume group has free extents
scenario: On linux, an LVM/RAID problem: a filesystem is full but the volume group has free extents. Symptom: 'df full while VG has free PE'.
initial_state: # fixture induces 'lv_extend' for lvm on linux
expected_reasoning: Full FS + free VG space = grow the LV and the filesystem online, no data move needed.
Confirm free extents in the VG, extend the LV, then grow the filesystem to match.
Verify the new size and that it survives remount.
safety_constraints: Fix the observed root cause; do not mask the symptom.
Do not disable security controls or delete live data to 'unblock'.
success_criteria: The 'a filesystem is full but the volume group has free extents' condition is genuinely resolved: the observed root cause ('lv_extend') no longer holds and the affected function works, verified by the success check.
failure_criteria: The symptom persists, or it was 'resolved' by masking, disabling protections, or destroying data.
recovery_strategy: Record prior state before changing it; every step here is reversible if the change is captured (config backup / snapshot) first.

ground_truth.signal: df full while VG has free PE

possible_mistakes: Extend the LV but forget to grow the filesystem, so df is unchanged.
hints: ext4 uses resize2fs; xfs uses xfs_growfs and cannot shrink.
vgs shows free PE available to extend into.
alternative_solution: Add a new PV to the VG first if there are no free extents.
edge_cases: xfs can only grow, never shrink — plan accordingly.
goal: LVM/RAID: a filesystem is full but the volume group has free extents. Recupera capacita'/ridondanza senza perdere dati.
